courses.title: AI for Ethiopia
courses.summary: Start with AI basics and learn practical, responsible ways students and teachers can use it.
courses.description: A beginner-friendly course for Ethiopian students and educators. The first four modules include EFBI videos, complete written lessons, and practice questions. Modules 5–12 will be added only when their learning material is ready and reviewed.

lessons.title: Welcome to AI for Ethiopia
lessons.summary: Meet the course, understand how to study each module, and begin with clear expectations.
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
## Welcome

AI for Ethiopia is an introduction to artificial intelligence for students, teachers, and curious beginners. You do not need programming experience to begin.

## How each module works

Watch the EFBI video, read the lesson, and complete the short practice check. The written lesson contains the main ideas, so you can continue when video access is slow or unavailable.

## What is ready now

The first four modules introduce the course, explain AI, show practical student uses, and explore lesson-planning support for teachers. Modules 5–12 are still being produced and will not appear as finished lessons until EFBI reviews them.

## Learn with care

Ask questions, test ideas, and check important information. Never place passwords, identity documents, private school records, or another person's personal information into an AI tool.

questions.prompt: What should you do if the lesson video is unavailable?
options: Use the complete written lesson
Share your password to unlock it
Mark the lesson complete without learning
questions.explanation: Every module keeps its main learning in the written lesson so video problems do not stop progress.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Modules 5–12 is correct?
options: They are already finished
They will appear after EFBI produces and reviews them
Learners must create them
questions.explanation: Future modules should not be presented as complete before their material has been produced and reviewed.

questions.prompt: Which information should never be entered into an ordinary AI learning prompt?
options: A general study topic
A preferred answer format
A private password or identity document
questions.explanation: Passwords and identity documents are private and unnecessary for ordinary learning.

lessons.title: What is artificial intelligence?
lessons.summary: Understand AI in simple language, recognize familiar examples, and learn why its answers can be wrong.
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
## A simple definition

Artificial intelligence is technology that learns patterns from examples. It can use those patterns to predict, classify, recommend, or create something new. It does not understand the world in the same way a person does.

## AI in daily life

You may already use AI when a phone suggests the next word, a map estimates travel time, an email service filters spam, or an app recommends a video. AI can also help a learner organize ideas or practice a subject.

## Why AI can be wrong

An AI system learns from data created or collected by people. Missing examples, old assumptions, and errors in that data can affect its output. Some tools can also invent a confident answer when they do not have reliable information.

## Keep a person responsible

Treat AI as a tool, not the final decision-maker. You bring the goal, Ethiopian context, judgment, and responsibility. Check important claims with trusted sources before using or sharing them.

questions.prompt: Which description of artificial intelligence is most accurate?
options: Technology that learns patterns from examples
A person living inside a computer
A source that is always correct
questions.explanation: AI systems learn patterns from data and use them to produce outputs.

questions.prompt: Which is a familiar example of AI in daily life?
options: A phone suggesting the next word
A paper notebook
A chair without electronics
questions.explanation: Word suggestions are based on patterns a system learned from language examples.

questions.prompt: Why should an important AI answer be checked?
options: AI can sound confident while being wrong
Every AI answer is written by a teacher
Checking makes the internet faster
questions.explanation: Confidence is not proof, so important claims need reliable evidence.

lessons.title: How students in Ethiopia can use AI
lessons.summary: Use AI to study and create while protecting privacy, checking answers, and keeping your work honest.
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
## Use AI as a learning partner

A student can ask for a simpler explanation, create practice questions, compare two ideas, plan a study session, or get feedback on a draft. AI should help you think and practice, not replace your learning.

## Give clear instructions

State the task, add only useful context, and describe the answer format. Instead of saying Help me study, try: Create five short photosynthesis questions for a Grade 10 learner. Put the answers after the questions.

## Check the result

A clear prompt can still produce a wrong answer. Verify names, dates, statistics, quotations, scholarship requirements, and safety advice with a reliable source. Ask a teacher or qualified person when the decision matters.

## Protect privacy and academic honesty

Do not share passwords, identity numbers, school records, health details, or private information about another person. Follow your school's rules, write in your own voice, and explain meaningful AI assistance when required.

questions.prompt: Which prompt gives the clearest direction?
options: Help me study
Create five short photosynthesis questions for a Grade 10 learner
Tell me everything
questions.explanation: It gives a specific task, amount, subject, and learner context.

questions.prompt: An AI answer gives a scholarship deadline without a source. What should you do?
options: Apply using that date immediately
Verify it on the official scholarship website
Share it with everyone first
questions.explanation: Application requirements and deadlines should be checked against an official source.

questions.prompt: What is a responsible way to use AI for an assignment?
options: Submit its answer without reading it
Use it to practice, then write and check your own work
Give it another student's private records
questions.explanation: AI can support practice, but the learner remains responsible for understanding and checking the work.

lessons.title: How teachers can use AI for lesson planning
lessons.summary: Draft useful lesson ideas with AI, then adapt every result for learners, curriculum, safety, and local context.
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
## Start with the learning goal

AI can help a teacher brainstorm examples, draft a lesson outline, create practice questions, or suggest different explanations. Begin with the subject, learner level, available time, and the skill students should demonstrate.

## Treat the output as a draft

Check every fact, answer key, quotation, and instruction. Adapt language, examples, and activities for the Ethiopian curriculum, the classroom, learner needs, and available materials. Remove anything inaccurate or unsuitable.

## Protect students

Do not place student names, grades, disability information, behavior notes, phone numbers, or other private records into an AI tool. Use fictional or anonymous examples when testing an idea.

## Keep teaching human

A teacher remains responsible for the lesson and for decisions that affect a student. AI cannot know the full classroom context, notice every learner's needs, or replace professional judgment, care, and feedback.

questions.prompt: What should a teacher provide first when requesting a lesson plan?
options: The learning goal and learner level
Private student records
A request to make every decision
questions.explanation: A clear learning goal and learner context help produce a more relevant first draft.

questions.prompt: What should happen before an AI-generated answer key is used?
options: A teacher checks every answer
Students receive it immediately
The tool promises it is accurate
questions.explanation: The teacher remains responsible for checking accuracy and suitability.

questions.prompt: Which information is safest to use while testing a classroom activity?
options: Real student health records
Fictional or anonymous examples
A list of student phone numbers
questions.explanation: Fictional or anonymous examples protect learners from unnecessary privacy risk.

articles.title: Why EFBI Academy starts with building
articles.excerpt: EFBI helps learners understand an idea, practice it, and turn it into something useful.
articles.bodyMarkdown:
Learning becomes powerful when it leads to action. EFBI Academy was created to give Ethiopian students a clear place to understand technology, practice safely, and build work they can explain with confidence.

## Start small and finish

A finished small project teaches more than a large idea that never becomes real. Each EFBI course breaks a subject into short lessons, useful checks, and a focused building task. Learners can see their progress and return without losing their place.

## Use technology responsibly

Technical skill matters, but judgment matters too. EFBI asks learners to check information, protect private data, explain meaningful AI assistance, and consider the people affected by a solution.

## Build for a real need

The strongest projects begin with listening. A learner identifies one clear school or community problem, creates the smallest useful version, tests it with sample information, and improves it from honest feedback.

EFBI courses are free. The goal is simple: help more students move from watching technology to using it thoughtfully, building with it, and sharing what they learn.
